findings.area: C: organizer obligations and ODR-V411-02 coverage
findings.finding: Amendment C still settles part of the organizer question itself and overstates how complete its scan is. (1) amendment.json declares R0.1-O1 ('must: The competition application's source implementation must begin at hackathon kickoff from a blank application repository or the organizer-approved equivalent') and the kickoff packet's 'empty/organizer-compliant' checks 'Met by its first branch', under OD-INDY-18. AMENDMENT C repeats this ('Some are met without any organizer'). Whether code authored before kickoff and written at T0 satisfies 'source implementation must begin at kickoff' is exactly the question STARTING-STATE leaves open. That code includes 7 implementation members, plus the generator output, the Conditor scaffold and the requirements import: 'An organizer could read the materialized contract declarations ... as material prepared before kickoff ... This policy does not claim that the F# contracts are exempt under every reading'. OD-INDY-18's quoted owner words do not decide R0.1-O1, and ODR-V411-02 does not ask about it. READINESS A meanwhile says 'No requirement is weakened or claimed met'. (2) STARTING-STATE says 'Every organizer reference in the frozen v4 inputs and the internal rule documents has a recorded disposition ... X19 scans for them and fails on any without one', and ODR-V411-02's impact says 'X19 lists every organizer reference'. Both are false. CAUSA-DATA-CONTRACT-v1 section 10 step 8 is a v4 source that the inventory cites 6 times, and it reads 'Before competition, verify organizer permission for pre-created dataset and app-specific executable schemas'. v4 risk-register RISK-12's mitigation reads 'Owner obtains it before the event (ADRP-016)'. DOMAIN-TEST-MATRIX section 29 ('Before kickoff, verify event rules regarding pre-written executable tests') and PRODUCT-REQUIREMENTS:1056 bear on the pre-written layout assertions that v4.1.1 writes at T0. None of these has a disposition, and ODR-V411-02 does not mention them. As a result, the owner's decision on the organizer conflict is posed over an incomplete list, and one 'must' obligation is resolved by the agent.

findings.area: B: X17 line scan and baseline binding
findings.finding: The line scan's comment and string stripping does not follow the F# lexer. Five of the new probe forms go undetected (x17r2.fsx). A string containing '(*' blanks every line up to the next '*)'. A char literal '"' or a verbatim @"\" swallows the keyword that follows on the same line. A triple-quoted '(*' and a module-level record expression are also missed. The byte-equality guarantee reads contractBaseline.package, a field of amendment.json that nothing binds to amends.package (which X20 pins to requirements-compiled/v4.1) or to APR-V41-OWNER-4. In mutX17, setting it to requirements-compiled/v4.1.1 and adding a hidden 'module Hidden = let run ...' to IF41-APP behind '[<System.Obsolete("(*")>]' gives these results: ContractCheck builds with 0 warnings, X17 PASS and validation PASS on the second generation and on --check, and contract-classification labels 06-IF41-APP.fs 'specification: types and signatures only'. CI's 'diff -r v4.1/contracts v4.1.1/contracts' would still catch it, and the committed contracts are clean. Two overclaims remain: READINESS C ('X17's line scan is a heuristic that rejects any other code') and amendment.json V411-B ('X17 rejects any implementation member that is not on the reviewed allowlist').
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/review411-r2/scripts/x17r2.fsx (R2a-R2e NOT DETECTED); /tmp/claude-0/review411-r2/mutX17; V41Package.fs:1569 (baseline = contractBaseline.package, unchecked); analysis/amendment.json changes V411-B; docs/READINESS-V4.1.1.md:41
findings.remediation: In X17, require contractBaseline.package = amends.package and contractBaseline.approval = amends.approval, or drop the field and use amends.package. Optionally verify the baseline files against the approved manifest's per-file digests. Strip strings and char literals before block comments, and handle verbatim and triple-quoted strings. Reword READINESS C and V411-B.
findings.disposition: Fixed: the contract baseline must equal the amended package and its approval (offline control). The stripper follows the F# lexer: strings, characters, verbatim and triple-quoted strings, then comments, nested. Record expressions are code. The five new forms are offline controls. READINESS and V411-B now name byte equality as the guarantee and the scan as a heuristic.

findings.area: Owner decisions: neutrality and process around ODR-V411-02
findings.finding: Four problems. (1) STARTING-STATE ('Organizer approval of the prepared material (ADRP-016-O2) is not sought') and the STORAGE-008-O1 disposition ('is not sought') state option A of the pending ODR-V411-02 as fact. Options B and C both involve an organizer record. (2) ODR-V411-02's impact says 'X19 lists every organizer reference with ODR-V411-02 as the decision', but 7 of the 20 references name OD-INDY-18. (3) It also says 'Until decided, v4.1.1 cannot be approved', but owner-freeze.fsx approve only prints 'Note: still pending' and records the approval. (4) owner-freeze.fsx decide's pull-request body for v4.1.1 tells the agent to 'apply these decisions in requirements-compiled/v4.1 (FREEZE.md step 2), recompile v4.1'. That is the approved package, which must stay byte-identical. The question itself is otherwise neutral ('The owner's call'), and nothing records ODR-V411-02 or ODR-V411-01 as decided.

findings.remediation: Write 'the package as proposed (option A) does not seek it'. Correct the impact sentence. Make approve refuse while a requirement-conflict request of the same package is pending, or soften the sentence. Make the decide body name p.Dir.
findings.disposition: Fixed: (1) 'not sought' reads 'the package as proposed (option A) does not seek it'. (2) The impact sentence is corrected. (3) owner-freeze.fsx approve v4.1.1 refuses while a requirement-conflict request of v4.1.1 is pending. (4) The decide body names the package's own directory.
